transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Asha Mehta (Veridian Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Ravi Singh (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): walkthrough of Redwood console analytics and cost per route, discuss pilot, security docs and next steps.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Asha (Veridian): Hi, I'm Asha, head of ML at Veridian. we own model infra and near-production stuff.
[00:13] Liam (CTO): Liam here, final sign-off on infra and procurement side.
[00:16] Ravi (SRE): Ravi, SRE, I'll handle network and VPC access.
[00:20] Maya: Great. Diego will run the console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics and cost breakdown per route. we have about 45 minutes.
[00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Cool, jumping into the Console. first slide, per-route dashboards - the idea is that each API route, e.g., /summarize, /chat, /embeddings, gets its own dashboard with token consumption, latency p50/p95, error rates, and cost buckets.
[01:05] Asha: when you say cost buckets, is that per-model or per-route? we have routes that hit multiple models depending on input size.
[01:12] Diego: good question. the breakdown can be by route, by model, and by tag. so if a route fans out to model variants, you get both the route-level and the model-level split. the billing export also includes per-token cost columns so you can attribute $$ back to teams.
[01:40] Liam: how precise is the token-level cost? we need this for internal chargebacks.
[01:45] Diego: we compute unit cost using model profiles: throughput, quantization settings, and inferred token distribution. it's within a few percent, but for absolute numbers we provide raw token counts plus the pricing slab you configure. billing export is CSV or parquet.
[02:10] Ravi: regarding data residency and PHI, if we go Dedicated or Private, how do analytics data and logs live? do they leave our VPC?
[02:18] Maya: for Dedicated you get isolated capacity and logs can be pushed to your SIEM. for Private (VPC/on-prem) the control plane can run in your network; we support push/pull audit logs and KMS integrations so keys never land in Redwood-managed KMS unless you opt-in.
[02:40] Diego: showing the per-route latency waterfall - you can see time spent in queuing, model inference, and network. this helps tune batching and priorities.
[03:05] Asha: we have some 1-2s p95 spikes on longer contexts - can Redwood show the effects of batching changes?
[03:12] Diego: yes, the console includes a suggested optimization panel - we call out batching, cache hit rates for prefix/KV cache, and quantization suggestions. the Optimize module can simulate throughput/cost impact if you change batch_size or enable 4bit quant.
[03:40] Asha: is that 'Optimize' product the same as Redwood Optimize? i've seen docs calling it Redwood Optima sometimes in my notes.
[03:48] Maya: yes, it's Redwood Optimize - docs sometimes get jumbled, sorry.
[03:52] Liam: on fallbacks: if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can we route to hosted or a cheaper variant? we need predictable SLAs but graceful degradation.
[04:02] Diego: that's built in: routing policies let you prefer Dedicated, then failover to Hosted or a cheaper quantized variant. you can define cost vs latency rules and automatic fallback.
[04:20] Ravi: for the pilot, we'd want to run route-level benchmarks with our real traffic. what's required from our side?
[04:27] Diego: sandbox VPC access and an example route list + sample payloads. we can run synthetic and replay tests. we'll also instrument the per-route dashboards during the run.
[04:40] Asha: we also need to see end-to-end cost attribution: e.g., call to /clinical-summary where prompt length varies widely.
[04:48] Diego: we capture input and output token counts per request (configurable retention window). for privacy you can mask PII and we can obfuscate payloads but retain token counts & timings for analytics.
[05:10] Maya: quick note on security: we are SOC2 and have KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO and RBAC. Diego will share the security pack after the call.
[05:20] Liam: we need network diagrams and evidence of encryption at rest/in transit for procurement.
[05:25] Diego: yes, will include network diagrams and key rotation details.
[05:30] Ravi: on costs - can the console break down costs by team or tag? we tag requests currently with X-team header.
[05:36] Diego: absolutely, per-route and per-tag cost aggregation is supported. you can define billing groups and export aggregated monthly cost per group.
[05:50] Asha: any limitations for streaming responses? some of our chat agents stream token-by-token and we prefer low latency.
[05:58] Diego: streaming is supported, and latency dashboards include streaming vs non-streaming. note that streaming increases total token count slightly due to chunking but we show both counts.
[06:20] Maya: i'd like to demo the cost explorer now, Diego?
[06:25] Diego: sure - opening the Console. (screen share noise) here is the route list, you can click a route and see token heatmaps by hour, per-model usage, and cost. see this spike at 11am - that's when your batch jobs hit.
[06:50] Asha: that's helpful. can we set alerts for unusual cost regressions?
[06:55] Diego: yes, budgets and regression alerts tie to eval prompts; we can alert on sudden unit cost increase or quality drop based on your evaluation sets.
[07:15] Liam: how do you handle model rollouts? we want canaries and automatic rollback if eval flavors degrade.
[07:22] Diego: rollouts support canary % splits, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback rules. you can wire eval triggers so if quality drops beyond threshold we pause rollout.
[07:40] Asha: about quantization suggestions - do you recommend per-model or global? some models lose clinical terminology with aggressive quant.
[07:48] Diego: Optimize gives model-level recommendations; for clinical models we default conservative quant and suggest performance trials. we'll add a 'do not quantize' tag for sensitive models.
[08:05] Ravi: network egress and billing - if we use Dedicated in a cloud region, do we still get detailed per-token cost even if egress billing happens separately?
[08:15] Diego: yes, the console shows Redwood service cost per token; cloud egress costs are separate but we provide an export you can join with cloud billing to get full stack cost.
[08:35] Maya: quick Q from procurement: do you have templates for SOC2/PIA for health customers?
[08:40] Diego: we have a healthcare pack and compliance add-on; will share the docs.
[08:45] Asha: timeline - we're targeting a pilot in early April and decision by end of April for Dedicated commit.
[08:52] Maya: that's our suggested timeline. we'll send pricing and sample contract language.
[09:00] Diego: demoing the CSV export - here's per-route daily cost lines: route, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, unit_cost, total_cost. you can slice by tag.
[09:20] Asha: great. can you also show how the dashboards look when you enable KV cache? we've heard that prefix caching can cut token costs for repeated queries.
[09:30] Diego: yep - enabling KV cache shows cache hit rate and estimated token savings. in one customer case we saw 18% token reduction on average for their FAQ route.
[09:48] Ravi: any caveats for cache and private deployment? we need cache to be inside our network.
[09:54] Diego: for Private, KV storage can be customer-hosted; for Dedicated we keep cache in isolated infra with encryption.
[10:10] Maya: circling back to next steps: Maya will send pricing, Diego will share security docs, and we schedule pilot.
[10:18] Liam: procurement will review; i'll send legal contacts.
[10:22] Asha: i'll prepare route list and sample payloads for the pilot.
[10:27] Ravi: i'll set up sandbox VPC and give access.
[10:30] Maya: perfect. any remaining questions?
[10:34] Asha: one last: do you support per-route token caps/rate limits? we want to cap expensive routes to avoid cost spikes.
[10:40] Diego: yes, you can set per-route quotas and throttles; we also support dynamic routing to cheaper models when thresholds hit.
[10:52] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the package and a recording.
[10:57] Liam: thank you, looking forward.
[11:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional name misspellings possible; product names: Redwood Optimize / Console / Dedicated sometimes abbreviated.
